Wash up and clean up
Friday 13 November 2026 · one 40-minute lesson · Year A
Term theme: Identity & Belonging
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
Objective
Wash up / clean up after an activity.
Source: scheme_references/BUILD_SOW.xlsx; BUILD Weekly - Autumn, C138. Strand and Friday slot confirmed by the owner.
Big question and success checks
How can I leave the space ready?
Follow the steps to wash up. Clean the work space with the right cloth. Check the work and ask for help when needed.
Evidence

VOCATIONAL-BUILD-A2-W02-E1: A dated observation of each learner washing an item and cleaning a work area after a water-transfer activity, recording actions, prompts, safety support, unfinished steps and a next step.
Prepare

Prepare an accessible supervised station: stable tray, unbreakable cup and spoon, a small amount of clean water, wash area, fresh rinse water, draining rack, separate clean cloths for dishes and surfaces, and handwashing access. Staff check the water temperature, prepare approved detergent to its instructions and keep containers out of reach. Prepare one set per learner and a separate model set; allow one supervised washing turn at a time.
Calendar and progression
Year A. Autumn 2 Week 2: 9–13 November 2026. Friday 13 November 2026, one 40-minute taught lesson. No clock time is specified. Weeks 1–6 are formative; Week 7 is assessing.

Independence / vocational strand. The community-project strand is not used. Week 1 plans a snack; Week 2 practises washing up and cleaning after a task. This does not teach the later recipe objective.
Careers
This helps me care for kit and leave a shared space ready.
Teaching sequence
Slide
Min
Teaching action
Read the objective, question, theme and careers line.
Offer a pause, chosen response mode and usual aid. Record any access help.

With stable trays, each learner moves a little clean water from cup to tray using an unbreakable spoon for about one minute. No drinking, food, dyes or sensory additives. Stop spills promptly. The resulting used items and wet space give the clean-up task a real purpose.
Read the objective and three success checks. These are formative teaching tasks.
Use the separate adult model set. Model clearing, washing, rinsing, draining, surface cleaning and handwashing. Staff control water and products.
Show a clean but wet cup and a dry storage space. Ask: “Put it away now, or let it dry first?” Expected: let it drain and air-dry, then check it is dry before storage.
Each learner has a supervised turn: wash one item, rinse, drain and clean their work space. Record individual actions; retain unfinished turns.
Finish the observation record; safely complete or recheck short steps. Rehearsal is not practical completion.
Give one prompt and brief retry. Leave wet kit to dry; adult checks floor and products. Wash and dry hands.
Accept a correct sequence step. For a floor spill: stop, keep clear and tell the adult; the adult manages the spill. Do not send the learner to find or mix a product.
Keep the word mat available and explain words in the task.
Hidden staff brief. Read the practical boundaries and key before teaching.
Hinge response and reteach

Show a clean but wet cup and a dry storage space. Ask: “Put it away now, or let it dry first?” Expected: let it drain and air-dry, then check it is dry before storage. If unsure, model the safe position on the rack and recheck with a wet spoon. The adult manages any remaining drying and later storage.
Routes

Supported: Use one step card at a time, an adapted grip or a stable tray. Allow pointing to request help. Staff can support an action with consent; record exactly what the learner did and what the adult did.
Independent: Follow the wash, rinse, drain and surface-cleaning sequence with the agreed adult safety checks. Check the work and request help as needed. Adult safety supervision still applies.
Aspire: Complete the same task, explain why dish and surface cloths stay separate, and spot an unfinished step. Improve that step with adult approval; do not handle products or hotter water.
Safe teaching and evidence
Boundaries and practical support

Staff complete the setting’s practical risk check and adapt equipment and access before teaching. Use only unbreakable items from a clean-water transfer task; no raw food, blades, glass, heat or electrical equipment. Adults prepare and handle cleaning products, check safe water temperature, change dirty water and manage spills promptly. Learners never mix or dose products. Use separate dish and surface cloths. Detergent cleaning is not disinfection; staff complete any required disinfection separately under the setting’s procedure. Keep chemicals secure. If the task is unsafe, stop and seek help. A dry rehearsal is an access alternative, not evidence of completed washing.

Allow a supervised turn for each learner to wash one item, rinse and drain it, then clean their own work space with the separate cloth. Staff control water, detergent and spills throughout. Record individual steps while observing. For a small group, allow about three minutes per turn; prepare extra supervised stations or record unfinished turns if group size or needs require more time. Do not imply that watching a peer proves a skill.

The six-minute evidence stage can extend individual observation. If all turns cannot be safely completed within the lesson, record the unobserved steps and plan a later opportunity. Watching, sorting cards or an adult finishing the task does not demonstrate the learner’s practical action.
Evidence and feedback
A dated observation of each learner washing an item and cleaning a work area after a water-transfer activity, recording actions, prompts, safety support, unfinished steps and a next step.

Wash up: step cards
First wash, rinse and drain. Then clean the space and check.
Point, say, draw, write or use an aid. Ask for help or a pause.
Only use the kit and water the adult has checked. The adult handles the soap and all cleaning bottles.
Step
What to do
1 · Clear
Clear the used kit. Ask the adult where water goes.
2 · Wash
Use the dish cloth and soapy water. Wash each side.
3 · Rinse
Use clean water to take the soap off.
4 · Drain
Place the item on the rack. Let it dry.
Wait for your turn. Ask for help. Leave wet kit on the rack; do not put it in the cupboard yet.
Clean the space and check
Use a fresh cloth for the work space. Keep it apart from the dish cloth.
Step
What to do
5 · Clean
Use the cloth and solution the adult gives you. Wipe the work space.
6 · Check
Check the kit, space and floor with an adult.
7 · Hands
Wash your hands with soap and water. Dry them.

Staff answers and observation
Wash up and clean up
These are guides for teaching, not prefilled learner evidence. Use a separate adult model. Accept a suitable alternative with a reason. Record access help and content prompts.
Model and task key

The water task is done. I clear the tray. An adult checks the water and adds the soap. I wash each side of the cup. I rinse it with clean water. I put it on the rack to drain and dry. I use a fresh cloth to clean the work space.
Step
Look for
Clear
Used items moved safely; learner asks where to empty clean task water.
Wash
All surfaces of an item washed with the prepared solution; actual learner action recorded.
Rinse and drain
Soap rinsed off in fresh water; item left safely on rack. Adult changes water as needed.
Clean space
Separate clean surface cloth used; surface wiped. Staff finish any required disinfection separately.
Check and hands
Learner checks the space, communicates a concern or help request, then washes and dries hands.
Storage
Wet items remain on rack. Staff arrange later storage once dry. Do not mark later storage as learner evidence unless observed.
Hinge and reteach

Show a clean but wet cup and a dry storage space. Ask: “Put it away now, or let it dry first?” Expected: let it drain and air-dry, then check it is dry before storage. If unsure, model the safe position on the rack and recheck with a wet spoon. The adult manages any remaining drying and later storage.
Common errors

A quick rinse is not the same as washing. A wet item is not ready for storage. Dish and surface cloths are separate. Looking clean does not prove disinfection. Adult completion, peer performance and dry rehearsal must not be logged as the learner’s washing skill.
Practical protocol and evidence
Before and during the lesson

Prepare an accessible supervised station: stable tray, unbreakable cup and spoon, a small amount of clean water, wash area, fresh rinse water, draining rack, separate clean cloths for dishes and surfaces, and handwashing access. Staff check the water temperature, prepare approved detergent to its instructions and keep containers out of reach. Prepare one set per learner and a separate model set; allow one supervised washing turn at a time.

Staff complete the setting’s practical risk check and adapt equipment and access before teaching. Use only unbreakable items from a clean-water transfer task; no raw food, blades, glass, heat or electrical equipment. Adults prepare and handle cleaning products, check safe water temperature, change dirty water and manage spills promptly. Learners never mix or dose products. Use separate dish and surface cloths. Detergent cleaning is not disinfection; staff complete any required disinfection separately under the setting’s procedure. Keep chemicals secure. If the task is unsafe, stop and seek help. A dry rehearsal is an access alternative, not evidence of completed washing.

With stable trays, each learner moves a little clean water from cup to tray using an unbreakable spoon for about one minute. No drinking, food, dyes or sensory additives. Stop spills promptly. The resulting used items and wet space give the clean-up task a real purpose.

Allow a supervised turn for each learner to wash one item, rinse and drain it, then clean their own work space with the separate cloth. Staff control water, detergent and spills throughout. Record individual steps while observing. For a small group, allow about three minutes per turn; prepare extra supervised stations or record unfinished turns if group size or needs require more time. Do not imply that watching a peer proves a skill.

Give one specific prompt and allow a brief safe retry. Record first performance and retry separately. Leave wet items on the rack. Staff arrange later storage once dry and complete residual cleaning; do not rush drying to claim completion. End with handwashing and drying after any further cleaning.
Evidence decisions
A dated observation of each learner washing an item and cleaning a work area after a water-transfer activity, recording actions, prompts, safety support, unfinished steps and a next step.

Record what was observed, response mode, prompts, adult actions and gaps. Suggested statuses: observed with stated help; partial; not yet observed. Do not award a total, infer a qualification result or turn a blank sheet into evidence.
